newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST - Davids profit seen climbing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST - Davids profit seen climbing.

text.p: Emerging independent grocery wholesaler and retailer Davids Ltd should report stronger full year results on Tuesday, analysts said.
Investors and analysts alike were keen to discover how Davids' acquisition of the 96-store chain, Jewel Food Stores would affect the company's bottom line.
Davids' acquired Jewel for cash and shares worth A$115 million in October last year.
"Jewel should produce cost savings and synergy, but there also has been some expenditure in refurbishing and expanding the chain's operations," one Melbourne-based analyst said.
Analysts forecast Davids' year after-tax pre-abnormal earnings to rise 17.5 percent to about A$53.6 million, from A$45.6 million in the year to June 30, 1995.
The final dividend is seen unchanged from 1995's five cents per share level for a total payout of 10 cents in 1995/96.
In July this year, Davids successfully completed a takeover of Queensland-based wholesaler QIW through a scrip offer which valued the company at about A$150 million.
The synergy benefits of this acquisition should flow through to Davids' earnings this financial year, analysts said.

Analysts said apart from its retail food chains Clancy's, Rainbow and Jewel, Davids was now Australia's largest grocery wholesaler, a leader in Australia's food service industry and owned 50 percent of the country's largest liquor distributor. "Davids is well placed to compete against Coles Myer and Woolworths and its earnings growth should be sustainable in the medium term," said a Sydney-based retail analyst.
Davids shares closed three cents firmer at A$1.69 on Monday.
Since June 30, 1995, Davids shares have risen 38.5 percent from A$1.22. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
